title: Directional stride–swing coupling fails to establish incremental Parkinson prediction across public gait collections
abstract: We tested a signed cross-variable timing statistic: the difference between forward and backward lag-one correlations of stride duration and swing fraction, averaged across feet. Source-only logistic models trained on31 gaitndd participants were applied without recalibration to151 gaitpdb participants, excluding both known identical opposite-label recordings. Signed lagged stride/swing-fraction cross-correlation asymmetry did not establish incremental external Brier benefit: delta +0.001792, joint95% interval [-0.014985,+0.013820], in31 source and151 target participants. AUC changed from 0.673281 to 0.646704. This exploratory reused-data analysis does not establish equivalence or absence of physiological information.
